newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - July 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - July 11.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Friday's electronic version of The Wall Street Journal:
* Falcon Drilling agreed to merge with Reading & Bates, forming a new company.
* MCI said its losses for entering local phone markets could hit $800 million this year.
* Ousted Apple Computer CEO Amelio said that despite the slide in the computer maker's earnings, market share and stock price, he did a good job as CEO and chairman.
* Boeing is in talks with Lockheed Martin on a private pact to safeguard sensitive data they shared as partners.
* Investors pumped an estimated $18 billion into stock funds in June.
* Top retailers sales rose 4.6 percent for stores open at least a year.
* Compaq posted a 58 perecent jump in quarterly profit before a charge, and announced its was lowering prices on business PCs.
* General Electric 's profit rose 13 percent to a record $2.16 billion.
* J.P. Morgan s quarterly profit fell 15 percent.
* R.J. Reynolds Tobacco is dropping its Joe Camel campaign.
* American Express said it is folding its discount brokerage business into its money-management operation.
* The FCC is expecting to let winners of wireless telephone licenses pay in annual installments instead of quarterly, a move to help the firms pay billions of dollars owed to the government.
* Marvel will merge with Toy Biz.
* Bond prices ended slightly higher Thursday, as reports from U.S. retail chains suggested that consumer demand remained moderate last month.
* In anticipation of a single European currency, investors have made profits betting on the once-weak bonds of the so-called Club-Med countries of Europe's sun belt: Italy and Spain.
